matches.stipulation: Scaffold match for the CWC Southern States Championship
matches.note: Both men fell from the scaffold locked in a piledriver attempt; Reaper was ruled the winner for landing on top of Walker in the safety net below.

name: Georgia Cup Tag Team Tournament (Day 1)

date.source: The document's own dateline framing; only part one of two for day one of a three-day tournament is in the held record.

notes: Warren Worthington III withdraws from his own tournament match rather than team with an American partner; Commissioner Bob Lane names David Smith as the injured Volcano's own replacement for Heat Wave '98.

name: Heat Wave '98

date.source: Combines the fed's own published card (grw-heat-wave-98-card, 19 August) with part two of seven of the broadcast itself (23 August); the remaining parts, including the Worthington/Smith four-on-four match itself, are outside this pass's own pull.

notes: A four-on-four elimination match teams Warren Worthington III with 'The Iceman' David Smith, Jimmy Lane and Cyrus Whitney against Logan Gunz, Byron Brady, Marc LeRoux and a mystery partner, per the fed's own published card; the match's own result is not in the held record. Part two witnesses a separate six-man elimination bout (Thunderstorm and the German duo of Van Kampen and Lehmann vs. Chicago Clash and Apocalypse Now) ending in a double count-out, and Commissioner Bob Lane forcing Worthington into the earlier four-on-four by threatening his contract.

name: Friday Night Showdown

date.source: The promotion's own next newsletter (7 November 1999) reports this broadcast under its own "11/5/99" results heading; the four-part posting itself carries a 7 November posting date.

matches.note: The champion blinded the challenger with his own powder pouch before finishing him with a superkick; the referee had been knocked out mid-match.

Denny Langham, the scheduled tag partner, refused to wrestle after striking the promotion's own commissioner backstage; "The Panther" Jared Mathys filled in for him under a standing 30-day services arrangement. Langham returned mid-match to attack Ferguson and abduct the champion's valet at ringside, letting Legend finish Gunz with a DDT.

no_appearances_reason: The card also carried a six-man tag match and a mixed-tag run-in not individually structured here; only the title match and the storyline-central angles above are structured.

evidence.source: The promotion's own four surviving parts of the broadcast, now served in full.
evidence.note: A memorial segment for the promotion's own late foreign talent coordinator turns into his son's public break with management; the Georgia State Champion's title rival strikes the commissioner and kidnaps the champion's valet; the Atlanta City Championship is retained in a bloody main event.

notes: The promotion's own late foreign talent coordinator's son, Jacob Moore Jr., uses his father's memorial tribute to accuse the promotion of ruining his father's imported talent, then unveils a masked protege of his own; the Georgia State Champion's title rival kidnaps the champion's valet after a tag match in which a masked wrestler filled in for the rival's own missing partner.

name: Sunday Night Slam

date.source: The promotion's own next newsletter (also dated 7 November 1999) reports these results under its own "11/7/99" heading; the broadcast frames the four matches shown as taped "earlier today."

no_appearances_reason: Four undercard matches are shown only as brief highlight clips with one-line results (per the promotion's own newsletter: Frankie Cash defeated Rowan Draper; Brian Rich defeated John Rose by forfeit; Justin Hvizdzak defeated Tony Wright; Jared Mathys defeated Kurt Dreamer); none is structured here, per the no-bulk-mirroring rule.

evidence.source: The promotion's own broadcast, now served in full.
evidence.note: A highlight-clip recap show; its centerpiece is a taped promo from the Georgia State Champion's rival, gloating over the previous show's kidnapping.

notes: Continues the promotion's own kidnapping angle with a taped promo; the four highlighted matches are also reported, one line each, in the promotion's own newsletter of the same date.

date.source: The promotion's own newsletter, dated 7 November 1999.
